Minimum Supported Erlang Version The minimum supported Erlang version for this release series is 27.0. RabbitMQ and Erlang/OTP Compatibility Matrix has more details on Erlang version requirements for RabbitMQ. Nodes will fail to start on older Erlang releases. Changes Worth Mentioning Release notes can be found on GitHub at rabbitmq-server/release-notes. Core Server Bug Fixes The basic.cancel notification sent on a consumer delivery timeout now properly clears consumer state even if the client does not respond with basic.cancel-ok. Most clients do not respond, and nodes older than 4.3.0 do not accept a client-sent basic.cancel-ok at all. The server now advertises whether one is supported, and a short timeout removes the consumer if the client never responds. A new rabbitmq.conf setting controls what happens on such a timeout: # notify_consumer (the default) sends basic.cancel to clients that support # the consumer_cancel_notify capability and closes the channel for others # close_channel always closes the channel, which is the pre-4.3.0 behavior consumer_timeout_response = notify_consumer GitHub issue: #17734 Classic queue expiration (x-expires) timestamps were lost on node restart, so the queue TTL timer did not fire when it was supposed to if the TTL outlived the restart. GitHub issues: #17708

entries.text: RabbitMQ 4.4.0 is a new feature release. Breaking Changes and Compatibility Notes The following AMQP 0-9-1 headers are no longer parsed: x-amqp-1.0-properties x-amqp-1.0-app-properties x-amqp-1.0-message-annotations x-amqp-1.0-footer RabbitMQ 3.13 and earlier used them to carry the AMQP 1.0 sections of a message received over AMQP 1.0. Nothing has written them since 4.0, so only a message stored by a 3.13 or earlier node and not read since carries them. Such a message is still delivered, with these headers converted like any other x- header rather than restored as AMQP 1.0 sections. Likewise, the x-basic-delivery-mode, x-basic-priority and x-basic-expiration message annotations are no longer parsed. They were written before 4.0 when an AMQP 0-9-1 message was encoded as AMQP 1.0 for a stream, so only a stream entry written by a 3.13 or earlier node carries them, and reading it no longer restores those three properties. OpenID Connect discovery responses are now validated more strictly. A deployment whose identity provider serves non-HTTPS (http://) endpoints, or whose issuer claim does not match the discovery endpoint used to retrieve it, will fail discovery validation after the upgrade. This is known to affect Cloud Foundry UAA, whose issuer is its token endpoint URL rather than a prefix of its discovery endpoint. Core Server Bug Fixes Deleting an exchange did not delete the bindings that pointed to it as a destination. A few related cases around auto-delete exchanges, transient queue cleanup and virtual host deletion were fixed along the way. GitHub issues: #17255, #17257 Quorum queue continuous membership reconciliation could add more replicas than the configured target. GitHub issues: #17310, #17311 Certain malformed urn:uuid: correlation or message ID caused exceptions during message format conversion. Such values are now rejected. GitHub issue: #17328 An operation that refers to an unknown queue type now fails with a precondition_failed channel exception instead of an exception and abrupt channel termination. GitHub issue: #17327 Classic queue recovery counted some message store references more than once. GitHub issue: #17351 x-max-age values are now compared as durations, so redeclaring a stream with 1D when it was declared with 24h no longer fails
